text.p: DonTech, a partnership between units of Ameritech Corp and Dun & Bradstreet Corp, is being restructured, with the result that certain D&B revenue and operating income will be shifted from the 1997 fourth quarter to the third quarter, D&B said Wednesday.
The restructuring will be accomplished through a series of agreements between D&B's Donnelley subsidiary and Ameritech advertising services.
DonTech was formed in 1991 by Ameritech and Donnelley to act as yellow pages publisher for Ameritech PagesPlus directories in Illinois and northwest Indiana.
D&B said DonTech has rescheduled numerous directories in order to smooth out inefficiencies.

D&B said the impact of the changes on its 1997 full year results is not expected to be significant, but about $30 million of revenue and operating income will be shifted from the fourth quarter to the third quarter.
D&B, changing the way it recognizes profits from its interest in DonTech, said revenue and operating income will now be recognized at the time of the advertising sale.
Previously, it recognized revenue and operating income when the directories were published.
